fields.essence: This is the energy of creation itself, the force that begins everything and is always beginning again. In you it makes what was not there before, in a shape no one else could have made. When it is moving you are more alive than at any other time: the work has light in it, something in you has to come out, and bringing it out is a joy. It arrives in its own time and leaves the same way.
fields.glance:
This is the energy of creation itself, the force that begins everything and is always beginning again. In you it makes what was not there before, in a shape no one else could have made. When it is moving you are more alive than at any other time: the work has light in it, something in you has to come out, and bringing it out is a joy. It arrives in its own time and leaves the same way.

In balance, this power has no fear of mistakes. Nothing new has ever been made without hundreds of wrong turns, so you begin before you know how it will end. What you are making will move one way and then another as it comes into the world; let it, because it has a life of its own. Your part is to be there when it happens, with a light hand, the way a midwife is there for a birth. By the time it is finished it has made you as much as you made it, and that is where the beauty is.

There are stretches when nothing comes, and they belong to this power as much as the making does. What comes next is being made in you where you cannot see it, and it needs you quiet, mostly on your own. Asking what is wrong with you is the one thing that makes the quiet last. Let it be, rest, and it comes back the way it left, all at once, carrying what it made in the dark.
fields.iching:
You are at the start of something, and the whole of its life is still ahead of it. Everything that begins passes through four seasons: it springs up, it grows, it is gathered in, then it is tried to see what it was worth. What you are asking about belongs to the whole cycle, not to this part, so look at all four from here. Nothing is yours until it has come through the last, and that takes longer than any beginning expects.

What it asks of you is to keep going, never to force. The sky moves through the day and the night without straining, which is why it never wears out. Make yourself strong the same way, a little every day rather than all of it in one blaze. Keep the pace of what is unfolding, slow when it is slow and fast when it is fast. Before you set out, be sure who you are and where you came from, because a force this size carries you a long way in whichever direction you are facing. The one danger in it is going too far. A strength like this can burn what it has made before it has taken shape.

In the body this energy is the head. Notice where you are holding yourself now: high, behind the eyes, already looking at what comes next. A beginning is felt there before the hands get any of it. Hold yourself the way the sky moves, steady and unhurried, with nothing in it strained. Heaven over Heaven: the sky, and under it the sky again, with nothing that gives way. Its creature is the dragon, which sleeps the winter at the bottom of deep water, wakes in spring, comes up into the open field and climbs into the sky. The traditional character shows vapour rising off wet ground under a strong sun, and the same word said another way means to parch. The Creative
fields.gene_keys:
Entropy Freshness Beauty Met, this energy is a fire, and what comes through you is alive the way a flame is alive. One morning the colour is back in things, and the joy has come with no more warning than sadness ever gave. With it comes something that has to be said or made, in your voice or with your hands. You take the step nobody has taken, and even when it fails you are out of the place you were shut in, which was the point.

Where it does most is a small room: a family, a few people who work together. Give it its moment and the whole room wakes. Then leave sooner than seems polite, because fresh things do not keep, and the one who lit the room can drain it by staying too long. The ones who carry this well are soft rather than hard, plain rather than shiny, because a fire is delicate and burns whoever grabs at it. Your strength is being able to be alone, trusting your own timing over anyone's. This energy goes flat some days, and the days go flat with it. You reach the end of one tired and cannot say what it was for. The word for it is numbness. Numbness is a feeling, though almost nobody knows they are in it, and knowing is most of the way out. You will do nearly anything rather than feel it, reach for the phone or call someone, and each works for about a minute.

Put a hand on your chest and notice what is there, even if it is nothing. Nothing is what it is meant to feel like at the start, so let it stay, with no pressure on it to change. It is not comfortable, nor is it meant to be. It is a gap, and a life needs its gaps. A bored child is not asking for a list of things to do, only for the blank to be seen, and you are the same. A fire begins as kindling that looks like nothing, then a breath on it. The flat you feel is the kindling, and your noticing it is the breath. Everything you look at is beautiful. A face, or a grey week in winter, shines with being exactly what it is, and the light is the same in all of it. It is so delicate that one word cracks it. A student once sat a whole dawn on a mountain beside his teacher, and when the sun rose he said one word, beautiful; the teacher afterwards called him a noisy fellow. The moment you say a thing is beautiful you have stepped outside it, so you say less and see more.

This is the fire when there is no longer anyone it is happening to. Even the flat days are beautiful from here, because they were part of it. All you can do is live it where people can see. Some will resent you for it, and some will come to stand in the light.
fields.human_design:
Self-Expression In the body, this energy is the pressure to make things your own way. Gate 1 is the door it comes through: the drive to put what is inside you out where it can be seen, in your shape and nobody else's. Nobody taught you the style. It is the one you had as a child, before anyone told you how things are done. When there is nowhere for it to go you are miserable, without always knowing why. When it does get out, the people near you feel more like themselves for having seen it.

From outside, doing it your way every time can look like stubbornness. What is going on is simpler: the making and the self are one movement, so asking you to do it the usual way is asking you to be someone else. The cost is that you are misunderstood more than most, and a hard word about the work lands like a hard word about you. People who carry this all their lives learn that being different was the strength all along, and that trying to be original on purpose is the one thing that chokes it.
fields.tarot: This is a family of two, the smallest kind there is. The other is Ancestors Bloom, the same fire a season on, with a harvest standing round it. Here it is the first catch, with nothing to burn yet and needing nothing. There the heat has something to feed, something to give away, and what it throws off keeps only while it is going somewhere. What both know is what a fire costs: while it burns everyone gathers, when it drops to a flicker you are nobody, and forcing it back up is how you end up making bargains with yourself. Open it when the beginning has caught and you want to see what the burning was for. Up in the sky the dragon climbs into, one face waits for it.
fields.body:
In the body this energy is given to the liver, and the reason is spring. The liver is the organ of spring: it is the first to wake in the year, it starts the growing, it keeps the life in you moving through the whole of you. When the liver is at ease, everything in you moves. When it is tight, everything waits. It is also the part of you that plans ahead, the general of the body, choosing which way the season will go. That is the work of the creative force too. It begins the season and sets the direction. The liver is where the body does the same.

Of everything inside you, the liver alone can make itself again. Lose most of it to injury or surgery and within months it has grown back to full size, working the whole time. The energy that begins things was given to the one organ that can begin itself again. It sits under your ribs on the right side, about the size of a small loaf. Rest your hand there and you are resting it on the part of you that starts over. The spark you were born with has a substance in you, and the substance is lysine. You cannot make it; your body takes it in, from meat or beans, or goes without. It is the same with the fire in you. On a morning when yours has dropped to a flicker, nobody notices you, and nothing you do by force brings it back. What brings it back in you is being fed, from outside and in its own time.

While it burns, everyone wants to be near you, and what you have then is a fire with something to feed. That is the same fire a season on, gathering a harvest round it, and in your body the two are made of one thing. Push it up by will and you pay, in what you give up to keep it lit. Fed, it comes back to you on its own.

fields.essence: This is the energy of the ground: the part of you that takes in whatever is given and turns it into growth. It refuses nothing. A seed, a stone, rain or a dead leaf, all of it is received, and what can grow from it grows. In a life this is the stretch when your work is to hold what has come to you and let it become what it is going to be.
fields.glance:
This is the energy of the ground: the part of you that takes in whatever is given and turns it into growth. It refuses nothing. A seed, a stone, rain or a dead leaf, all of it is received, and what can grow from it grows. In a life this is the stretch when your work is to hold what has come to you and let it become what it is going to be.

Carried well, it is a quiet kind of strength, the strength of being able to bear a thing without needing to change it first. Things come to you now when you stop going out to get them, so the work is to make room. What you do from trust gives everyone more, and what you do from fear takes from everyone, yourself first. The moves that matter are small, made by feel, and most of them look from outside like doing nothing.

The way is to let it come. There will be days when it feels as if you have been left behind and ought to be making something happen, and the ground has an answer to that: everything that has ever grown has grown out of it, and none of it was hurried. Stay soft, stay where you are, and receive.
fields.iching:
You have been given something to carry through, and the carrying is the whole of the work now. It is not yours to start, because it was started before it reached you, and it is not yours to steer. What it asks is the strength of the mare: she can run as far as any horse and still she runs behind, along the ground, going where it goes. Set out in front and the way is lost at once. Come behind, and the one worth following shows.

What you are carrying has a whole life ahead of it, from its first showing to its last test, and your part belongs to all of that, not to this stretch alone. Keep to your own kind while it lasts, the ones who grow things and wait for them. The ones who charge ahead you will lose for a while, and losing them is part of it. Soft at rest, firm the moment it moves: that is how the ground is, and how you can be. Rest in what is steady and it goes well.

In the body this energy is the belly, the soft front of you that takes in what it is given and carries the weight without ever being told how. Notice where you are holding yourself now. Let the belly go, sit as the ground sits, and hold to what was handed to you until it is done. Earth over Earth: the ground, and under it the ground again. Whatever falls on it is taken in, and whatever is set into it comes up in its own time. Its creature is the mare, who runs as far as any horse and runs behind. The traditional character sets the sign for earth beside a sign for stretching out: ground as far as you can walk, giving under every step. The Receptive
fields.gene_keys:
Dislocation Orientation Unity Met, this energy becomes finding your way by being carried. You stop steering and the ground begins to move you. Things start to line up on their own: the person you needed turns up, or you find you are in the right town without having planned it. None of that can be forced, because it happens when you are not looking, and it happens in spite of you. Your timing sharpens until being out of step registers in your body as plainly as hunger does, and your own face begins to show.

What you do with it for other people is the strange part. To set someone on their way you give no advice, because advice they can get anywhere. You sit with them wanting nothing from them, letting them see your weakness as much as your strength, and in your company they find out that being afraid is safe. Nothing had to be done. Harmony is catching, and a person who has stopped fighting their own life steadies the room they are in. This energy has a low, and the low is the feeling of having stepped off the world. You stand on the same ground as everyone else and it does not seem to hold you. Somewhere a wrong turn was taken, you cannot say where, and since then you have been out of place in every room. Most often it comes out as busyness: the days fill, the load goes onto your shoulders, and the hands stay moving so the hollow underneath cannot be heard. The usual move is to change the outside, a new plan or a new town, and the relief lasts about as long as the unpacking.

You have never left the ground. You cannot, and no turn you took was wrong. The feeling is real as a feeling and false as a fact. It changes the moment it is felt all the way through instead of outrun. Let it soak in, the way rain soaks into a field. What you were running from was the longing for home, and the longing is the first sign of the way back. You are home, and you know it. The seeking is over, and it ended by finding that there was never a distance to cross. There is the ground, there is you, with no line where one stops and the other starts. Two people standing together are already a third thing, the pair itself, so there was never a two on its own. Being home is ordinary, the plainest thing you have ever felt, and it holds everything.

This is what being carried becomes when the one being carried lets go. Nothing leads now and nothing follows. Life goes on moving and you are the ground it moves over, the way the seasons move over a field. It leaves the world exactly as it is, with every mystery in place, and puts you in the middle of your life, where you had been all along.
fields.human_design:
Direction of the Self In the body, this energy is the pull that gives a life its direction by receiving it. Gate 2 is where it enters: the part of you that knows which way your life faces, the way a field knows which way is downhill, by taking in what falls on it and letting it run. It does not make the road. It feels where the road already goes, and what belongs on it is drawn toward you. Asked why you are going that way, the honest answer is that it is the way, and you cannot always say more than that.

From outside, a person moved like this can look like someone waiting. Nobody can see a direction being received, so they see the not-deciding and call it drift. The cost runs the other way: the pull is to take everything on alone and settle for less than you wanted, because you did not trust that support would come. People who carry this all their lives learn to let the direction arrive, and to let the help in with it.
fields.tarot: This is a family of two. The other is Odyssey of Freedom, the self that stops imitating and shows its own face. What the two share is water. There is a sadness in water, a longing for the sea it came from. Both of you know it. Here it is the ground that lets the water soak in, and there it is the water that will not be told what shape to take. Open it when you have been carried far enough to wonder who is doing the travelling. Three faces stand at the edge of the field the mare runs and one of them is looking for the road.
fields.body:
There is one bone in you that everything comes to and nothing leaves from: the breastbone, the flat bone down the middle of your chest, about the length of your hand. The collarbones come to its top, the ribs come to its edges from both sides, and it goes out to nothing. It holds the whole front of you together by being where things arrive, which is this energy's whole work. That is the work of the ground too: it starts nothing, everything is set into it, and it carries what it is given. The breastbone is where the body does the same.

Of everything in you it is the bone that is moved by everything and moves nothing itself. Rest two fingers in the notch at its top, between the collarbones, and breathe in. It lifts, then settles. Nothing in you can move it on purpose. The ribs carry it, a dozen or so times a minute, and have since your first breath. You are resting your fingers on the part of you that is carried. The trust this energy runs on has a substance in you, and the substance is phenylalanine. You cannot make it. Your body takes it in, from meat, eggs or beans, or goes without. Part of it is built into you as it came. The rest becomes what wakes you, what moves you, then the colour of your skin and hair. Trust, too, is a chemistry: it is made in you slowly, let out while you relax, never decided.

What you let all the way in goes into the body as chemistry, not as a thought, which is why the body can feel carried before you have understood a thing. As you are carried into a wider life, your own face begins to show. In you the quiet carrying and the face that shows share one substance. The more you give way, the more comes through you.

fields.essence: This is the energy of a beginning, the moment something new is alive in you and does not yet have a shape. A seed lies in the ground the whole winter, alive, with nothing above the ground to say so, and that is where you are now. You can feel how real it is without being able to say what it will become.
fields.glance:
This is the energy of a beginning, the moment something new is alive in you and does not yet have a shape. A seed lies in the ground the whole winter, alive, with nothing above the ground to say so, and that is where you are now. You can feel how real it is without being able to say what it will become.

In balance, this energy takes its time. Whatever you begin, you begin on strength stored up beforehand, against ground that does not give. The first tries fail, and the failing is not the end of anything. Each one puts strength into what is coming, so what finally comes through lasts longer than anything that came easily. You make small moves and let them be rough. The ones that hold become ground for the next. There is more power in a new thing than looks possible. A shoot, when the rain finally wakes it, will split a rock.

Nothing about this is orderly, and it is not meant to be. What looks like chaos is only what a beginning looks like from inside it. There was never any chaos, only the difficulty of starting. The hard part is the not-knowing. It asks to be settled early, and settling it early is the one way to lose it. A thing pushed to be finished before its root has gone down goes flat. Build slowly and stay steady, because when the breakthrough comes it comes all at once.
fields.iching:
A beginning is under way in you, and this is the hardest part of it. Two things have met in you for the first time, the push to move and the weight above it. The difficulty is nothing more than that meeting. The storm has built and the rain has not come down. What you have begun belongs to the whole cycle ahead of it, the growing, the gathering, the trial, not only to this rough first part. Disorder is how everything starts. Order comes after, a little at a time.

What it asks of you is to stand firm where you are. Do not set out toward the goal yet, because from here it cannot be seen. Take the loose strands of what you have and twist them into one cord you can hold. Give people real charge of the parts you cannot carry, and keep the ground you have found. Your mind leads the body the way a ruler leads a country, so set it right before anything else. Hurrying is the one thing that turns difficulty into danger.

In the body this energy is the foot and the ear: the foot that steps first, the ear that hears what is coming before the eye can see it. Notice which of the two is louder in you now. Hold yourself the way a seed holds under the ground, with the root going down while nothing shows, because the root is what the whole plant will stand on. Water over Thunder: clouds built up overhead, and under them a shock in the ground, the first movement that wakes what was asleep there. The storm is full and the rain has not fallen. The traditional character is a picture: a blade of new grass above the line of the ground, and under it a root drawn longer than the shoot. Difficulty at the Beginning
fields.gene_keys:
Chaos Innovation Innocence At its best this energy makes something new out of what is changing, and your hands are busy with it. Clear a space and something grows into it. That is how life works, and it is how you work. You try a thing, then the same thing a little differently, the way a child sorting buttons into boxes stumbles on a new game. Most of the tries fail. The failing is not a mistake but the trying, and it goes on until one holds. What you are making is not made alone. What is around you gets in and changes the work, then changes you, so you keep updating where you stand. You can feel that it all fits before you can see how. It is the best feeling you know.

The order you are looking for is already inside the mess, the way the tree is already inside the acorn, and the work is letting it out. Keep the best version of the thing in view and give the energy to that, because this much energy with nothing to serve will drive you mad. At its lowest this energy is the fear of change, and the fear closes the hands. Whatever you rely on, the people, the house, you hold as if holding could make it stay. It works for a while, since a thing held still looks like safety. The chaos you dread is rarely a storm. It is an undercurrent, a low unease that lives in the belly and never quite settles. When one of the things you hold is threatened, the unease comes up, and what it shows is not a new disorder but how hard you have been holding all along. The usual move is to find something else to hold before the old one gives way, so the fear never has to be felt. Changing everything around you does not touch it. You were made to change, and every part of you is afraid to.

The word for it once meant open space, and fear turned it into disorder. Stay with the unease where it lives and it shows what it is: a love that has not gone the whole way yet. Love a little further, and the hands open on their own. At its height this energy is the innocence of someone who has been through everything and opened again. A newborn has it without knowing. So does the old woman whose heart came open after a long life, and the only difference between them is that she knows. No one is in control, and the child in you has always wanted to find out what happens. The hands are open because there is nothing left to guard.

Turned loose into a fresh field, even old cattle jump like calves, and that is what this is: the joy of filling an empty space with your own dance. You know how it ends, nobody knows the road, and the road is the play. You can grieve on the outside and watch it go on underneath. What you were looking for at the heart of everything turns out to be love.
fields.human_design:
Ordering In the body this energy is the pressure to bring something new into a shape it can live in. Gate 3 is where it comes in: the drive that takes what has never existed and tries form after form until one holds. It can see the pattern in a mess where other people see only the mess. It runs in you as an urge to get the raw thing into some order the moment it arrives, and the order never comes in a straight line. A new thing takes time to take root, the way a child takes years before it can do a day's work, and the waiting is where you doubt yourself. The pressure is to force it early, to push too hard or speak too soon, into a world that is not ready for it.

From outside the trying looks like disorder, and you are misunderstood more than most. People who carry this all their lives learn that what they bring lands when the time is right, not before. The timing is as much the genius as the idea.
fields.tarot: This card belongs to a family of six that hold one whole life between them. This one begins it. The others are the watching and the cutting away, then the return and the feeding, then the finishing. What the six share is a trust in what looks like a mess. The mess is where life finds its next shape. Every one of them knows it from a different point in the life. Open any of them to see that trust further along. Here it is the first breath. Clouds and thunder, the rain not yet down: five faces wait in that weather.
fields.body:
In the body this energy is given to the navel, and the reason is birth. For nine months everything that fed you came in at that one point, from a supply you did not make. In your first minutes the cord was cut, and the opening closed itself. From then on you did for yourself what had been done for you, on nothing but what you had been given. Just under it, low in the belly, is where the energy you started with is kept, the root that everything after grows from. Everything you have begun since has begun the same way: fed before it could feed itself, then cut loose, with only what it had been given to live on.

Press a finger straight into your navel and it meets a firm floor at once, the scar that closed the opening. Press a finger's width to either side and the wall gives, because there is only belly behind it. Rest a finger on the firm point and you are resting it on the first beginning you ever made. The energy that begins things has a chemistry in you, shared with its kin, and the substance is leucine. You cannot make it; your body takes it in, from meat, beans or milk, or goes without. There is more of it in you than of any other piece you are built from, about one in every ten. What begins in you is built of what you were fed, taken in from outside, none of it made by you.

Life goes on changing, and as it changes it takes with it what it has just left. In your body that is chemistry before it is anything else. What you are becoming is built of the same substance as what you were, and the change runs on what you take in. What stops changing in a body is dying.

fields.essence: Not knowing is where this energy begins: the young mind standing in front of something it cannot yet make sense of, wanting to. It is the state every person is in before they understand anything, and it is honest, because a mind that knows it does not know can still be taught. It comes up whenever something new stands in front of you, a person you cannot read, or a turn in your life you did not see coming. It stays until you understand, which is never as soon as you want.
fields.glance:
Not knowing is where this energy begins: the young mind standing in front of something it cannot yet make sense of, wanting to. It is the state every person is in before they understand anything, and it is honest, because a mind that knows it does not know can still be taught. It comes up whenever something new stands in front of you, a person you cannot read, or a turn in your life you did not see coming. It stays until you understand, which is never as soon as you want.

Carried well, this mind knows what it is for. It is for understanding, for saying what it understands, never for deciding. Logic can argue either side of anything, and a mind handed the deciding argues itself into whatever it was afraid of. Being sure in the head has never once made a body feel safe. What this mind is really after is not knowledge. Knowledge is what it thinks it needs to take the unease away, and all knowledge can give is the hope of peace. Understanding is another thing, and it does not live in the head.

The pull, when something will not make sense, is to ask why, then ask again, hunting the reason that will finally let you rest. No reason ever has. One answer is replaced by the next question, and that restlessness is the whole of the folly. The way through is not a better answer. Let the asking wear itself out, keep the mind at what it is good at, and understanding comes up on its own, from lower down than the question, once you are tired enough of answers to live inside the question for a while. You will not stop thinking. You will stop asking.
fields.iching:
Something has come up that you do not understand, and you are the young one here, at the foot of a mountain with the water just out of the ground. Everything that has ever grown was covered like this once, before it knew what it was. You are ready to learn without yet knowing what you need. The one thing you can feel clearly is the wanting to know.

What this asks of you is to go and ask. Find the one who knows the ground, ask them once, and mean it. The first answer is the clear one. Ask the same thing a second time, then a third, and you are no longer asking. You are stirring, and every stir clouds the water until nothing can be read in it. Take what you were given and carry it off without another word. Then do the plain things well while it works in you, each one through to its end, because a character is built out of small things finished.

In the body these two forces are the hand, which holds a thing steady, and the ear, which takes in without needing to see. Hold still and listen. Notice where you are holding yourself now. There is real danger under you, the danger of not knowing, so stop at the edge of it and do not go down alone. Mountain over Water: a spring coming out of the ground at the foot of a mountain. The water is clear at its source and has no idea yet where it is going. The mountain above stops the view, stops the water spreading, so it gathers there. The traditional character shows a plant under a cover: something growing where it cannot yet be seen. Youthful Folly
fields.gene_keys:
Intolerance Understanding Forgiveness Understanding is what the water does when it is finally left alone: it runs clear on its own. It has nothing to do with knowledge. Knowledge is what the mind thinks it needs to take away its unease, and all it can give is the hope of peace, which is what keeps you asking. Understanding comes after the mind has looked at a thing from every side and found that every side can be argued. It is the way a riddle with no answer is given to a mind: at the moment the mind sees its logic will never solve it, something gives. Then the answer arrives as a feeling in the whole of you, up through the body from the belly, and the question is finished with.

The mind is let off the job of settling your life, which it was never fit for, and set free for what it loves: looking at patterns, turning them over, playing. You see both halves of any argument and take neither. You understand people the same way. The restlessness is still in you. Now it points outward, toward what could be put right in the world. Intolerance begins as a slant on the mind's own logic. The mind has a bad day, decides it does not like someone, and by evening it has a list of good reasons. Under the reasons is a feeling, with logic wrapped round it, and the logic measures only what it was sent to find. That is how an opinion turns into a certainty, a resentment into a conviction, until you are blind with your own reasoning and cannot see that you are. Out of reasons come blame, justification and guilt, the whole furniture of a world split into sides.

Sit alone in a room for an hour with nothing to do and it shows itself closer to home: most people cannot bear their own minds. Under all of it is fear, thrown onto other people and defended from behind an argument. Look at the other side of your own opinion, honestly, and you will find the fear it was standing on. The mind was given a job it cannot do, which is to make you safe, and no amount of being sure in the head has ever made a body feel safe. Forgiveness is a warmth that goes through the borders between people and finds there was never a debt on either side. Nothing was personal. The part of the mind that needed a reason for what happened has died. In its place is a plainness that watches the old story and does not pick it up. There is nothing restless left in it. You cannot do it. It comes when you are tired enough of the drama, lands like a surprise, and something in the chest that had been choked comes open. Then it runs backward, down the line of the people you came from, untying what they left tied, so that debts which stood for generations are cancelled at the source. The water has gone on past the mountain now, and anyone can drink.
fields.human_design:
Formulization Gate 4 is the pressure to make sense of things: the part of you that takes a pile of loose facts and finds the shape they make. It does not rest until something fits. In you it runs as a mind that puzzles at everything, that has to know how a thing works before it can leave the thing alone, and is happiest when a pattern finally closes. What it makes is an answer, and the answer is how this mind tries to make life safe. Every answer is a guess that fitted. Held as a possibility it can be dropped the moment a better one comes, and a mind that can drop its answers stays light.

From outside, a person built like this gets called a know-it-all, the one with an answer for everything, and is often wrong while sounding sure. The pull is to act on an idea the moment it arrives, before it has taken root, then to doubt yourself when it does not take. The idea was not wrong. It was early. Watch which of your answers the world goes on to prove, and let the rest go.
fields.tarot: Four make up this family that works out how people manage to be together. One is the yes that goes all the way in. Another is the closeness that breaks through a guard, and the third is the gathering that gives a crowd its shape. This one is the mind in the middle of it. It is the part of a bond that wants reasons and has to learn to do without them. What the four share is union. Here it is the reason nobody had to give. A spring under a mountain draws a crowd of faces, and most of them are teachers.
fields.body:
The neocortex is where this energy lives in you, and the reason is youth. It is the thin folded sheet over the outside of your brain, the newest part of it in the history of animals, and the last part of you to finish: the front of it, where your judgement is made, is still being wired into your middle twenties. Everything it knows it took in from outside you. It is where your words are made, and every reason you have ever given for anything. That is the young mind's work in you too. It asks, takes in, holds what it was given. The neocortex is where your body does the same.

What this layer of you has learned it cannot put down. Look at any word on this page and you cannot see it as marks. The meaning arrives before you can stop it, in a fraction of a second, doing what took you years to learn. Now try to un-read it. That is the first answer, gone into you, and there is no asking it out again. The mind that cannot leave a question alone has a substance in you, and the substance is valine. You cannot make it. Your body takes it in, from milk or meat, beans or oats, or goes without, and when it builds a protein it folds valine into the middle, away from the water. The change this energy is moving toward is written in you there too: a child born with it has a mind that does not run riot, from the first day.

The reasons you give for not being able to bear someone are made of the same substance in you as the closeness that gets through a guard and the yes that goes all the way in: one chemistry in you for how people manage to be together. Take this energy out of you and there would be no reasons between you and anyone, no expectations and no blame.

fields.essence: This energy is the wait for something already on its way. It is not the waiting of someone with nothing: the strength in you is whole, and what you are waiting on is real. From inside it feels like a full sky before rain, heavy, near, not yet falling. In a life it is the space between the asking and the answer, when nothing you do will bring the answer closer.
fields.glance:
This energy is the wait for something already on its way. It is not the waiting of someone with nothing: the strength in you is whole, and what you are waiting on is real. From inside it feels like a full sky before rain, heavy, near, not yet falling. In a life it is the space between the asking and the answer, when nothing you do will bring the answer closer.

Certainty is what it becomes when it is carried well. What you are waiting for does not come when you call it; it comes when it calls you, and it will. Waiting and patience are not the same thing. You can wait either way, but only one of them rests. Act from resolve and the timing holds. Act from hurry and everything lands a beat off, however good the plan was. The pull is to check, to open the oven to see whether the bread has risen, when every opening lets the heat out. It rises in the dark with the door shut.

Let the hour come to you, and stay inside your days while it does. There will be a stretch when it feels as if nothing is holding anything together, as if the whole arrangement would stall the moment you stopped pushing. It does not stall, because you were never the one holding it. Rest where you are, stay with what is near you, and let what is coming find you.
fields.iching:
You have done everything that was yours to do, and the thing you are waiting on has not moved. That is the situation, with no weakness in it. You are strong, the strength is ready, and in front of it is a danger you cannot push through by being strong: a river too high to cross today, a person who has not decided. The timing belongs to the sky, which takes no instructions. Whoever crosses the great water crosses it after the long wait, when the crossing is sure.

What it asks of you is to be sure of the thing and to stop looking for the sign. Truth is what makes the waiting hold: if what you are waiting for is real, the light stays on while you wait. Keep to the ones who can wait beside you without talking about it. Eat, drink, sit at the laid table as the wise do while they wait; the rain finds a rested person ready.

In the body this energy is the head and the ear. The head stays up and clear while the rest of you is made to sit. The ear hears the change before the eye sees it, so stop watching the sky and listen. Stand the way a farmer stands at the door with the seed in, under a sky that has not broken. Nothing about it is idle. The one move made to hurry the rain fails; every small move made while it holds comes good. Water over Heaven: the rain has gathered in the sky over dry ground and has not come down. Under it the strongest force there is stands waiting, a force that could push through anything but this. The old character sets rain above someone stopped beneath it, made to wait for what only the sky can give. Waiting
fields.gene_keys:
Impatience Patience Timelessness Let a thing take the time it takes: that is the whole of patience, and it can be learned. It takes patience to learn it, and it is the one skill that proves itself, since every wait that pays makes the next one easier. At first it is a technique: you notice the urge to force, you do not act on it, the unease stays a while, then the loop that fed it goes quiet. Done often enough it sinks into the body, and one day the body cools on its own, the way a mist comes up off a river to calm a hot afternoon. Nothing has changed and everything is easier. From there you hear the rhythms you were too fast to hear. Winter comes in a life the way it comes in a year, and passes the same way, on its own, when it is let.

Patience is trust when it is not being practised. Life keeps a pattern you are inside and cannot see the whole of; hindsight keeps proving it was there. Kindness comes from the same slowing, and so does love, because patience is what love sends ahead of itself. A tightness in you says that everything should already have happened, and the tightness is impatience. The reply is late, the light will not change, the thing on its way is somehow too slow. It feels like drive, it gets used as drive, and everything begun from it lands a beat off, because action out of agitation is never the same as action out of resolve. Under it is a fear older than anything that happened to you, the fear that nothing is holding the pattern together; a body tuned to that fear never feels safe, however much it arranges. Breath goes high and shallow. The whole of you braces like someone late. It is a dry afternoon spent watching a sky that will not break, and the afternoon gets longer the harder it is watched.

Impatience is not a flaw in you. It is your own rhythm gone missing, and a rhythm can be found again. Feel the restlessness instead of obeying it and it sinks on its own. Under it is the plain sense that life keeps its own time, and that you are inside that time, not outside it waiting to be let in. No one is waiting any more. The rain falls or it does not, and nobody in you is keeping count. Patience is gone along with impatience, because both need time to happen in, and time has stopped being the thing you live inside. Moods still come and go. The patterns that make up a person keep running, the way weather runs, while something has stepped out of the game and is not gripping any of it. This is very ordinary, quieter than the word makes it sound.

It is what patience becomes when even the one being patient lets go: the end of all fighting. Everything alive is waiting, and a life can be seen as one long wait for its end; from here that is not sad, only true. The strength that stood under the sky is still there, and so is the sky. The rain is falling on the field.
fields.human_design:
Fixed Patterns A day with a shape is what this energy needs in the body, and Gate 5 is the door it comes through: the part of you that wants its meals at their hour, its sleep at its hour, the same small returns every day. Discipline has nothing to do with it. This is older, from where the body keeps itself alive by doing the same things at the same times, and in you it runs as comfort in the repeated thing: the walk at the same time, the bed made before anything else. When the day keeps its pattern you have more of yourself for everything in it. When the pattern goes you feel it before you can say why.

From outside this gets called rigid, or afraid of the new. What is happening is that a rhythm is being kept, and the rhythm is what lets the rest of the life move freely. It goes wrong the same way from both ends, forcing order on the day by will or giving up on shape altogether. People who carry this all their lives learn to keep their hours without apology, and to stop asking anyone else to keep them.
fields.tarot: Four cards make this family, and each of them is the same strength held under something. Here it is held under a sky that has not broken. Ease in This holds it under a thin wind. Sol Star lets the ground come down to meet it. Lighter Than a Feather holds it under a mountain. What they share is a trust that what is held is not lost. Open any of them to see that strength held another way. Under a sky that is full and has not broken, five faces keep their places.
fields.body:
The body gives this energy to the sacral plexus, and the reason is that this is where you hold on. Against the inner face of the flat bone at the base of your spine a weave of nerves gathers, and out of it run the nerves of your legs, with the nerves of the doors below. What is behind those doors fills on a schedule you did not set. The weave carries the news that it is full, then keeps the door shut until the hour suits you. The engine that works you all day keeps itself here too, in the dark: it runs down by night, fills while you sleep, and is whole before you ask.

You are doing it now. Something below your navel has been filling since you last stood up, and this weave is holding it until the time comes. Put a hand flat on the base of your spine, on the bone between the hips. The weave lies just inside it, and you are resting your hand on the part of you that can wait. The stillness this energy asks of you has a substance in you, and the substance is threonine. It is one your body cannot make, so it arrives in what you eat, eggs or beans, or it does not arrive. Beyond what it builds, it sets in you how your cells take light in and turn it into something you can use. How much reaches you is set by how you live: fear closes it down, an open heart draws it in.

This substance is not this energy's alone; three others in you share it, and it does the same thing in all four. Anyone who has been in love knows what it does: the hours pass differently then, as if you had stepped out of time. Patience felt deep in your body does the same thing more slowly. It opens your heart, and the opened heart lets the light in.

fields.essence: Friction is the energy here, the heat that rises between two people the moment they come close. In you it is the pull toward someone and the flinch away from them, arriving together, out of one place. The flinch is not a verdict on the person. It is the old fear that you can be hurt at all, and it wakes whenever someone is near enough to matter. Every quarrel you have ever had began there, before a word was said.
fields.glance:
Friction is the energy here, the heat that rises between two people the moment they come close. In you it is the pull toward someone and the flinch away from them, arriving together, out of one place. The flinch is not a verdict on the person. It is the old fear that you can be hurt at all, and it wakes whenever someone is near enough to matter. Every quarrel you have ever had began there, before a word was said.

Carried well, this energy is honesty at the right moment. The true thing said too soon is a stone thrown; said when the heat has fallen, it goes in and does its work. You are not fearless, but you have stopped being afraid of the fear, so it no longer decides for you, and nobody near you can use it to move you. What looks like calm from outside is a person who can stand in the middle of their own alarm without leaving.

The way is to find the fear where it lives. It is in you, older than you, carried in the blood from people you never met, and whoever is standing closest only wakes it. Felt there, in you, it loosens, and the wall you built against them comes down on its own, because nothing behind it was ever in danger. The ones you have fought hardest are the ones who have brought you nearest to peace.
fields.iching:
You are in a dispute, your case is honest, and the other side has stopped listening. That is the whole situation: your truth is real and the door is closed. Nothing you say now will open it, because the two of you are moving in opposite directions, and every push sends you further apart. Nobody has ever come out of the far end of a quarrel holding the thing they went in for, and even a victory won here is taken back before long. Stop halfway. The middle of a quarrel is the only place in it where anything is settled well.

What it asks of you is a fair third person, someone with no stake in either side, who can say plainly what is being fought over so that it stops being about pride. It asks you to leave the great crossings alone, the move, the new undertaking, because the strength in the room is contradicting itself. Every dispute sits inside a relationship, and the person you are arguing with is one you will still live beside when it is over. Be firm inside, as the sky is, and give on the outside, as water does; giving here keeps the peace, which is no surrender.

In the body this energy is the ear, hollow on the outside so that it can take a thing in. Notice where you are holding yourself now: talking, or listening. Hold yourself as the water lies, low and open, so that what is said comes all the way in before you answer it. Heaven over Water: the sky above, going up, and the deep water below, going down. Two things share one place while moving apart, and the gap between them is the quarrel. The traditional character sets the sign for speech beside the sign for public: words that were kept inside, said where everyone can hear them. Conflict
fields.gene_keys:
Conflict Diplomacy Peace An open heart is tactful without trying, and that is what this energy becomes once the guard is down. It has nothing to do with the careful phrase, which anyone can learn and a shut heart can deliver perfectly. It is a sense, in the body, of where the other person is: how open, how braced, how near the edge. You feel a quarrel coming before it has a shape, and you can turn one word so that it passes. When someone comes at you hot, you take it in and hand it back with nothing added, so the heat has nowhere left to go. When you refuse the game of blame, the other person is left holding their own share, which changes them or moves them out of your life.

What this does between people is what falling in love is: the rub between two natures wearing through until nothing stands between them. The ones you are meant to open keep arriving, year after year, and each opening makes the next one easier. Being this vulnerable is the strength. Your heart is worn where anyone can reach it, and that is what lets you reach theirs. A feeling gets big enough and you stop having it: it has you, so that from inside it the other person looks like the danger. That is where every quarrel starts, two people who have both agreed to be their feelings for as long as it lasts. Underneath is one fear, older than any argument, that someone standing close can hurt you or take something from you. So you guard. The chest hardens and a small distance is kept going. The guarding was learned early, between the ages of seven and fourteen, so most of a life's strength can go into keeping it up without a day of it being noticed.

Think of the hardest relationship you have now. What that person seems to hold over you is a part of yourself you would rather not meet, and they are the only one who can bring it up. The fear was never in them. Ask what the quarrel is really about, and the answer is nearly always the part of you they bring out. The relationships that will not leave you alone are the ones holding the thing you have not yet felt, which is why they stay. Nothing is left to defend, because there is no one inside to be attacked. Where there had been two sides to keep even there are no sides now, and the evening-out that took such effort stops on its own. An old man rowing across a river was struck by another boat, turned to shout, and found it empty, drifting, nobody in it. The shout died in him. Live as the empty boat and nothing that comes at you arrives as an attack, since there is no one in you for it to land on. This peace was under everything the whole time. Stop and listen: it is there, in the birds, in the wind dropping. Even the wall of your own skin stops being a border, and you feel life moving in everything that lives. Nobody can take your life from you, because you are life.
fields.human_design:
Friction Closeness is what this drive wants, and the rub is how it gets there. Gate 6 is the door it comes through: the wanting to be near someone with the fear of being seen too closely, arriving as one pressure. When two people warm to each other a heat comes up that does not feel like welcome, a snag in the warming, and most people take the snag as proof the fit is wrong. It is not proof, only the place where two feeling natures touch, the edge that real contact forms against. In someone who carries this, the heat comes with closeness itself, quick or a slow simmer, and smoothing it away leaves politeness with nothing under it.

From outside it looks like someone who starts things. What is going on is that they feel the edge before anyone else and cannot pretend it is not there. The cost is being called difficult by people who wanted the warmth without the rub. Those who carry this through life learn that the rub was the way in, and that a closeness with no friction in it never got close.
fields.tarot: Inside the Ring of Alchemy, this code is the raw friction the work begins from. Its siblings, UL 40, 47, and 64, carry the rest of the transmutation: exhaustion turned to deliverance, oppression turned to transfiguration, confusion turned to clarity. The Magician's ring works with what is already at hand, nothing brought in from outside. Five Majors take up this card's argument. The codon ring gives one Arcana, the Magician, the worker who transmutes what is on the table. The two trigrams each give their own faces: Heaven above as the Fool and the Empress, the open beginning and the pressing abundance; Water below as the High Priestess and the Hanged Man, the listening depth and the patient suspension. What begins as a quarrel is refused a fight, and by the end it is only material on the Magician's table, waiting to be worked.
fields.body:
This energy is given to the nerves of your belly, the net over the gut, and the reason is that the belly knows first. Before a feeling of yours is a thought, it is there. Your gut has a nerve system of its own, with more nerve cells than your spine. The great nerve between your belly and your brain sends most of its news upward, so the belly has reported before the head has decided. When something threatens you, these nerves slow the gut and pull blood toward the muscles: that is the drop or the knot you feel in an argument before a word is said. The knot in you is a wave, not a verdict.

Bring to mind someone you have been avoiding, and the belly answers before the thought is finished. Then breathe out slowly, a hand laid flat below your ribs, and feel the same place let go. The nerves that tightened it are the ones that release it when your breath lengthens. Your hand rests on the part of you that felt it first. When the last wall in you goes, the body follows, and every cell makes peace with the others. That peace has a substance in you, and the substance is glycine, the smallest of the twenty pieces every part of you is built from. Your body makes it and takes in more from food, meat or the bones a soup is boiled on; it is sweet on the tongue. It has been found in the dust of a comet, one of the few pieces of you ever found out there.

The friction in you shares this substance with three of its kin, and together they turn a dark thing into a lighter one. That work begins in a body, in the belly, where what is raw in you is heated until it changes. Once started it spreads, one opening making the next, into the people near you.

fields.essence: Gathering is what this energy does: it takes people who are scattered and makes them one body that moves together. It is the reason a room settles when you walk into it, why people listen when you speak, even when they do not like what they hear, because your voice carries the sound of someone who can see where things are going. It does not push. It is felt as influence long before anyone would call it leading, and it lives in you whether or not you ever stand at the front.
fields.glance:
Gathering is what this energy does: it takes people who are scattered and makes them one body that moves together. It is the reason a room settles when you walk into it, why people listen when you speak, even when they do not like what they hear, because your voice carries the sound of someone who can see where things are going. It does not push. It is felt as influence long before anyone would call it leading, and it lives in you whether or not you ever stand at the front.

Carried well, this energy listens more than it speaks. The greatest guides are the ones who listen, and often a person who has been listened to properly finds their own answer with nothing added. It guides when it is asked, takes its time before it answers, and sometimes the best guidance it gives is none. What it wants for the people around it is that they need it less. A false leader holds on to you. A true one is quietly working to be rid of you, so that you can lead yourself.

The pull is toward being seen, and this energy does its work unseen, which is the hardest thing about carrying it. Recognition comes late to it or not at all, because it is always a little ahead of the crowd, and a crowd rarely thanks the one who was early. If you are holding it right, being thanked stops mattering. What you gather, you gather the slow way, drop by drop, like water under the ground that nobody sees collecting. One day it comes up on its own, and people come to it.
fields.iching:
Scattered strength is being called into one body, and the calling needs a centre. A crowd is not an army: loose strength wins nothing and breaks what is near it, while the same strength gathered round one it trusts can carry a whole country. The water is dangerous only while it is everywhere. Held under the ground, it is what the field drinks from.

What this asks is a seasoned hand at the centre, someone with the years to know when to advance and when to camp, trusted all the way by those above, level with those below. The army exists to keep the people safe and for nothing else. Raised for any other reason, it turns on itself. So the way to grow your strength is not to seize more of it. Be generous to the people, hold them the way the earth holds water, and the crowd gathers on its own. Two rules govern the whole thing: that the end is right, and that the manner is right, especially at the start.

In the body these forces are the belly, which carries the weight, and the ear, which hears what is still under the ground. Notice where you are holding yourself now. Sit as the ground sits over the water, open above with everything held below, and listen before you move. Earth over Water: the wide ground on top, and under it, in the dark, water gathered, waiting. Its picture is an army, a crowd of scattered people turned into one body that moves together around the one it agrees to follow. The traditional character shows a heap made whole: confusion turned into something that works. The Army
fields.gene_keys:
Division Guidance Virtue Guidance is help that does not impose. It never walks in uninvited, never presses an answer on someone who only needed to be heard, because its whole art is helping another person find their own road rather than taking the road over. Put your opinions aside, listen, and the one in front of you often finds the answer with nothing added from you. Sit with someone over tea, talk about ordinary things, and what they needed arrives out of the space between you. Sometimes the best guidance is none.

Carried like this, you lead from behind the throne rather than on it. You guide the energy in the room rather than the people in it, make a space where the people in it find their own order, then step back and let someone else have the light. People feel clearer about their own direction just from being near you, without your having said a word. What holds it together is trust in life to go where it is going, rather than taking hold of it. Division is the line that puts some people above others, and it runs so deep that it feels like the shape of the world rather than a choice. It sorts people into classes, sides, ranks, then teaches each of them to think in those sorts, so nobody can picture another arrangement. Some are made to follow, handing their authority to whoever sounds sure of himself. Some are made to take that authority and keep it. Both halves serve the same line, and the fear of losing power is what holds it in place. Like draws like here: stand at the level of someone waiting to be rescued, and you will draw exactly the leader who profits from keeping you there. Most of the people paid to help, the doctors, the teachers, would be out of work if you stopped needing them, and some part of them knows it.

There is nothing wrong with looking up to someone. It is a natural stage. The trick is to find the one who can truly listen, who takes in what you are carrying so completely that you finally dare to feel it, which is how it lets you go. Virtue is what is best in a person let out into the air, with nothing in them bent. It has nothing to do with being good on purpose, which anyone can perform. It is your nature going through you unimpeded, and its reward is itself, past any need to be seen, past even the need to be of use. It is delicate, and it cannot breathe where people speak ill of each other. Every day people do small unseen acts of it, and the power of those acts is past counting. They are what holds off the chaos. The old story says the world is made of shards of a vessel that broke, and every one of these acts sets a shard back. From here the whole long history of ranks reads as the world waiting to be put back together. A child raised among people like this needs no other teaching.
fields.human_design:
Collaboration Gate 7 is the pull to give a group its direction, the part of you that organises other people almost without trying. Put you in a room of scattered people and within the hour the room has a shape, without your having stood up. What you carry is not the hunger to be out front. It is the sense of where the whole thing is trying to go, with the knack for seeing what each person is for, so that the effort turns into one line of march. You are strongest beside the one at the front, the hand that directs the energy and holds the thing together, because a leader is only as strong as what stands behind them.

From outside it can look like control, or like a person who cannot take a suggestion. The cost runs inward: pushed toward the spotlight, this pull drains you, since being seen was never what it was for. People who carry it all their lives learn that influence done from beside is worth more than a title, and that the room follows the one who knows where they stand.
fields.tarot: Inside the Ring of Union, this code stands as the discipline of virtue, the gathering that learns to serve rather than divide. Its siblings, UL 4, 29, and 59, carry the rest of the work: the young mind finding understanding, the leap into the depths, and the dissolution that lets intimacy form. This is the family that governs how people come together cleanly. The Tarot reads this gathering through five faces. The codon ring gives one Arcana, the Lovers, the choice that joins many into one path. The two trigrams each give their own faces: Earth above as the Devil and the World, the binding that divides and the wholeness that completes; Water below as the High Priestess and the Hanged Man, the depth that listens and the pause that will not be rushed. The Devil binds the crowd first, the Lovers put the choice to it, and only then can the World make the many one.
fields.body:
This energy lives in the diaphragm, and the reason is the breath. The diaphragm is a dome of muscle across the middle of you. Every breath you take begins there: it tightens, drops, and the whole of you moves with it, lungs filling, belly rising, blood drawn up toward the heart. Nothing in you was told. One muscle in the middle moves, unseen, and the rest of you follows, which is what this energy does with people. Breathing low, everything in you is gathered round one centre. When the breath climbs high in the chest, the middle of you is straining after something, and the rest comes apart around it.

It runs without an order, twenty thousand times a day, and takes one when you give it. Hold your breath: you have commanded it. Let go: it leads you again on its own. Put a hand on your belly and breathe in. The belly comes out under your hand, and nothing in the belly did that. You are feeling the one in the middle that the rest of you follows. Guidance has a substance in you, and the substance is valine. You cannot make it. Your body takes it in, from meat or eggs, beans or oats, or goes without, and the muscle you move with takes it apart for itself instead of sending it to the liver. It is the same substance in the forgiving in you, the yes that goes all the way in, the closeness that gets through a guard: one chemistry in you for how people are together, made for people with nothing ranked between them.

Guidance arrives when you pause with someone, truly together, talking about ordinary things. While you sit like that, your body is already in it, below any plan to help. Leadership shared like that between people is what this substance in you is for.

keywords: A Way of Being Only Yours

fields.essence: Being yourself among other people is the energy here: what only you could be, finding the ones it belongs with. Most of the lives around you look alike, the same shape of week, the same wants, and the pull to match them was laid down before you were seven, when fitting in was the safest thing you knew. Under that is a way of being that cannot be copied, because the moment you plan it, it is gone. It is the whole of what you have to give, and it is enough.
fields.glance:
Being yourself among other people is the energy here: what only you could be, finding the ones it belongs with. Most of the lives around you look alike, the same shape of week, the same wants, and the pull to match them was laid down before you were seven, when fitting in was the safest thing you knew. Under that is a way of being that cannot be copied, because the moment you plan it, it is gone. It is the whole of what you have to give, and it is enough.

Carried well, this energy has no picture of itself. You do not decide to be different, nor decide to fit; you are in the world all the way, in an ordinary life, and still nobody could mistake you for anyone else. What comes out of you then is fresh, because it was never planned, and it is felt more than seen: in how you carry yourself, in the sound of your voice. None of it can be faked, and none of it can be learned from someone else.

The way is to stop chasing the ones you belong to. Think of a voice you know across a crowded room: you turn before you have made out a word. That is how the people who are yours find you, by the sound of you being yourself, and it works only while nothing is put on. Bring nothing sanded off. What you fear is being seen, and being seen is the way in.
fields.iching:
You are being drawn toward people, or they toward you, and the drawing is real. This is not a crowd thrown into one room; it is the quieter sorting underneath, each finding the ones it shares a life with, and it is recognised, never built. Before you go to it, put yourself three questions and answer them honestly: is what you bring great enough, will it last, will it hold? If it will, there is no fault in you, and the ones who have been unsettled will come to you from every side, one after another, as they make up their minds.

What it asks is that you force nobody and delay nothing. Whoever comes too late finds the gathering already closed, and that is the one hard edge in a gentle situation. Whoever holds people together does it from underneath, as the ground holds water, never by pulling; the strength is lent by the people who stand on it, and anyone who forgets that loses them. Give what comes to you away again, down through everyone, and the belonging lasts.

In the body this energy is the belly, with the ear above it: what you hear goes down into you and is kept, as the ground keeps rain. Notice where you are holding yourself now. Settle low, soften, and let what belongs to you arrive. Water over Earth: rain on open ground, going in. The ground drinks it and goes soft; the water spreads to every low place at once, so that the two stop being two. The traditional character is two people standing close together, one beside the other, and in old China it was also the word for a neighbourhood, five households under one head. Holding Together
fields.gene_keys:
Mediocrity Style Exquisiteness A leap of faith in yourself is where this energy turns, and what comes through after it is fresh. This has nothing to do with what you wear or how you live; it is the flowering of what you are, and it cannot be faked or copied, because it does not pass through the mind on its way out. You are yourself without wondering what anyone thinks, and the risk in that is only risk as other people count it. Something creative takes hold of you rather than the other way round, and once you have felt the freedom of that, whether it succeeds stops being the point.

From outside it looks dangerous, as nature is dangerous to anything that runs on rules: wild, unplanned, full of leaps. So it gets pushed to the edges, into art or music, where there is room for it. It does not need the edges. A person with this lives an ordinary outer life with a rebellious inner one, walks through the market with everyone else and still cannot be missed. Their freedom catches, and all they want is more people free. The dream stops being dreamed and starts being made. The lives around you look alike, and the pull to match them is a fear, the fear of being different, wearing the face of being sensible. It was taught, in the years when sameness was rewarded while difference was corrected, and by now it feels like your own temperament. It is not; it is a stereotype worn so long that it keeps you safe, and keeps everyone else safe about who they think you are. Under it you think what everyone thinks, want what everyone wants, and serve a machine that was here before you rather than the life you were given.

What you fear is not failing. It is succeeding, because to become what you are you would have to step past what everyone expects of you, and you do not know who you would be out there. So you dream of the lives you might have had, watching other people live them on a screen, moved and going nowhere. Every child gives off a light, and yours went dim a little at a time, so slowly that you never noticed the day it did. You have fallen in love with what you are, and it is not vanity, because everywhere you look you see the same thing in everyone else: each one a jewel, cut differently, none of them alike. Your nature is wild: nothing tames it, and you are never the same from one moment to the next, as fleeting as light playing through clouds. You lead no one, and you leave no tracks to follow; the people who try to copy you are the only strangers you know, since they are strangers to themselves. Water is weak, so nothing sticks to it, no plan, no grudge; you can rest completely, and resting is the last rebellion. A star at dawn, a bubble in a stream: it is all passing, and that is what makes it exquisite.
fields.human_design:
Contribution Something in you wants to add itself to the world, and to have it count. Gate 8 is the door it comes through: the urge to bring what only you see out where other people can use it, in your own words, and with it the pressure to know when. Not every room wants it, not every idea lands, so the person who carries this learns the hard way when to speak and when to keep the thing to themselves. What they are contributing, in the end, is not the idea. It is themselves, and the being is the whole contribution.

From outside it looks like someone who sets the fashion, who will not follow the crowd and does not seem to mind standing apart. What is going on is quieter: they cannot be anyone but themselves without their throat closing. The cost is being misunderstood by people who wanted them to fit, and the loneliness that comes of it. Those who carry this through life learn that trying to be a model for others, by becoming someone they are not, is the one thing that wears them out.
fields.tarot: This code belongs to the Ring of Water, and the family is small, only two. Its single sibling is UL 2, the pure receptive field. These are the two great feminine codes in the genome, one the open ground that receives everything, the other the unique self that shines by its own nature. Water finding its level and the diamond catching the light, bound by the same chemistry. Every face this card draws is about belonging, and they disagree about what it costs. The codon ring carries one Major, the Star, the hope drawn up out of the deep. The two trigrams each lend their own faces: Water above as the High Priestess and the Hanged Man, the one who perceives and the one who waits; Earth below as the Devil and the World, the bondage of false belonging and the completion of true belonging. The chain of fitting in comes first, the Hanged Man hangs long enough to see it for what it is, and the Star rises over a self that belongs to itself.
fields.body:
Of every organ, this energy is given to the thyroid, and the reason is the pace. Everything in you keeps one time, the warmth of your skin, the beat of your heart at rest, and one small gland low in your neck sets it, from inside every cell at once. It is two halves held as one by a bridge across your windpipe, about the weight of four coins. That is holding together as your body does it: every part keeping one time, because one thing set it.

You can feel the setting on a cold morning, in the warmth of your own hands, which is partly this gland's doing. Or rest two fingers on the inside of your wrist and count: fear can hurry the beat in a second, but the pace it returns to when you are still was set here weeks ago. It is in the sound of your voice too, in the timbre nobody else has. The self in you that cannot be copied has a substance, and the substance is phenylalanine, one of the twenty pieces every part of you is built from. You cannot make it; it arrives in food, in eggs or beans, or not at all. Once in you it becomes the colour of your eyes and the hormone that sets your pace. Deep in you it is one of two substances that move you toward your opposite, so that what you are finds what you are not, the two held in balance.

You change day to day, while the same substance is taken in and spent the whole way, as a river is never the same water yet is still the river. The part of you that receives whatever is given runs on it too, so the receiving and the self that comes of it are built from one thing.

keywords: Held by a Breath of Wind

fields.essence: This energy is the small step, with a great deal of power behind it. There is more strength in you than the day asks for, and the whole art of this is where you point it. Pointed at nothing it runs in a circle. Pointed at one thing you care about, it goes further than any great effort could, one plain step after another. In a life this is the long stretch made of small acts, the errands, the same tasks every day, which either add up or do not.
fields.glance:
This energy is the small step, with a great deal of power behind it. There is more strength in you than the day asks for, and the whole art of this is where you point it. Pointed at nothing it runs in a circle. Pointed at one thing you care about, it goes further than any great effort could, one plain step after another. In a life this is the long stretch made of small acts, the errands, the same tasks every day, which either add up or do not.

What it becomes, held well, is a track worn by repetition. Do a thing with your heart in it, then do it again, and a groove forms that the rest of your life begins to run down on its own. Every act counts, however small, because each one makes more of whatever it was done from: an act done in resentment makes resentment, an act done in joy makes joy. When the small acts lead toward the one thing you want, even the chores stop being empty, since each is a step on the way. Without that one thing, the steps are decided by whoever is nearest, and you follow the crowd without meaning to.

Everything turns on where you look. Look up at the whole mountain and the knees go weak. Look down at your feet, and one step is small enough to take, with the next one easier. At every real beginning, a new year, a new house, the first few steps set the groove for all the rest, so take them with the thing you want held close.
fields.iching:
A great force in you is being held by something far smaller than itself. Not blocked; held. The strength is real and wants to go, while the only thing shaping it is a breath of wind across the top, too light to stop it if it chose to break through. So the holding here is gentle, and it works by patience, by friendliness, by many small things kept, never by a show of power. The old king in this picture kept neighbours who wanted war calm by a steady stream of friendliness.

The clouds have thickened and it has not rained. Everything needed is present, the charge is high, and still it does not fall, because the moment has not come; forced, it would scatter. What this asks is to attend to the small. Tend the details that serve the larger thing, keep the outward things in order, your manner, the way the day is kept, and let the rest go. Be the shepherd who keeps a flock calm by the calm of their own mind, letting the sheep find their own grass, watching only that they are safe.

In the body this energy is the thighs under the head, the strength that walks, checked by what is thought above it. A warning is folded into the gentleness. Do not fall in love with the small advantage, because if small gains are all you take pleasure in, they are all you will have. Keep to the small with the great in view. When the rain comes, the holding is over. Wind over Heaven: the sky's own strength moves below, and across the top of it passes a breath of wind, not stopping it, only shaping where it goes. Clouds have thickened over the western fields and no rain has fallen. The old character for the name puts a field under stored grass with a cover over it: a small store, kept. Small Taming
fields.gene_keys:
Inertia Determination Invincibility Determination is one step, taken. The mind shows you the whole mountain at once and the knees go weak just looking, so you stop looking up. You look down at your feet, and there is a stone to step onto. That first step is the hardest, and it is also the easiest, because it is only one step. Every step after it is easier, and if you fall off the path, the first step is what brings you back. The stones lead off over the horizon now; you cannot see where, and it does not matter, because they are leading somewhere.

The word sounds like force, gritted teeth, a long war of will, and it is closer to the opposite. The more of it you have, the less effort it asks, because what you are building is a groove: a thing done with heart, then done again, until the energy of your life follows the track on its own and the practice seems to hold itself up. Only the first few steps ask for real strength. Small acts done with heart gather a momentum that stops being stoppable, and one morning you are halfway up without having noticed the climb. The small has got hold of you, and this is what it is like.
